requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol (`decmatch`) IS used for checking encoded payload fields.
requirements.original: The matching symbol MatchDecodedContent `decmatch is used for checking encoded payload fields.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol IS composed of the `decmatch` keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance.
requirements.original: The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:decoding-target
requirements.canonical: The mandatory template instance of a MatchDecodedContent matching symbol IS called decoding target.
requirements.original: The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:template-field
requirements.condition: the template field uses the MatchDecodedContent matching symbol
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses `decmatch` matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and the decoded instance is successfully matched by the decoding target.
requirements.original: A template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and if the decoded instance can be successfully matched by the decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` MAY specify one of the UCS encoding formats.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: If the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is present, the specified encoding format SHALL be used for the decoding trial.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or to the type of the decoding target.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be assigned' in a Restrictions list; chose the restrictive reading (only these types).
readings: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol MAY be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types (other types not explicitly excluded).

requirements.subject: ent:decoding-target
requirements.canonical: The decoding target of `decmatch` MAY be a template of any data type.
requirements.original: b) The decoding target can be a template of any data type.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

ambiguity.issue: The source text is garbled ('fields of r universal charstring types'), and restriction d) implies an encoding format also applies to charstring fields; chose universal charstring only, as literally written.
readings: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.
The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of charstring or universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be of charstring type.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` predefined function.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter value is not one of the strings allowed for decvalue_unichar
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time or a runtime error; chose 'an error' generically (compile-time if the value is known statically, otherwise runtime).
readings: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a compile-time error.
An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a runtime error when matching is performed.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter is missing
requirements.canonical: If the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is missing, the encoding format "UTF-8" SHALL be used.
requirements.original: d) If the template field is of charstring type or is of universal charstring type and the encoding format is missing, the default value "UTF-8" shall be used.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Before `decmatch` decoding, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to bitstring values using the predefined functions `hex2bit` and `oct2bit`.
requirements.original: At first, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to a bitstring value using the predefined hex2bit and oct2bit functions (specified in clauses C.1.18 and C.1.22) and charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Before `decmatch` decoding, charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.
requirements.original: At first, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to a bitstring value using the predefined hex2bit and oct2bit functions (specified in clauses C.1.18 and C.1.22) and charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Prior to `decmatch` decoding, the bitstring or universal charstring value is stored into a temporary anonymous variable.
requirements.original: Prior to decoding, the bitstring and universal charstring values are stored into a temporary anonymous variable.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding of bitstring values is performed by implicitly calling the predefined function `decvalue`.
requirements.original: Decoding is then performed by implicitly calling the predefined decvalue function (specified in clause C.5.2) for bitstring values and decvalue_unichar function for universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding of universal charstring values is performed by implicitly calling the predefined function `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.original: Decoding is then performed by implicitly calling the predefined decvalue function (specified in clause C.5.2) for bitstring values and decvalue_unichar function for universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: In `decmatch` decoding, the anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the decoding function.
requirements.original: The anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the function, the second parameter contains another temporary variable called decoded instance.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-instance
requirements.canonical: In `decmatch` decoding, the second parameter of the decoding function is a temporary variable called decoded instance.
requirements.original: The anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the function, the second parameter contains another temporary variable called decoded instance.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-instance
requirements.canonical: The decoded instance IS of the same type as the decoding target.
requirements.original: The decoded instance is of the same type as the decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: If the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is present, it is passed as the third parameter to the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: If the optional encoding format parameter is present, it is passed as the third parameter to the decvalue_unichar function.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding IS successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string after decoding.
requirements.original: Decoding is successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string (i.e. the whole encoded value has been successfully decoded).

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching mechanism produces an unsuccessful match if decoding has not succeeded.
requirements.original: The matching mechanism will generate an unsuccessful match if decoding hasn't succeeded.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.condition: the enumerated value has an associated value list in its definition
requirements.canonical: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list, the template SHALL reference the enumerated value name followed by a list of integer templates in parentheses.
requirements.original: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list in its definition, the enumerated value name shall be referenced followed by a non-empty list of integer templates in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-template
requirements.canonical: The list of integer templates following an enumerated value name in a template SHALL NOT be empty.
requirements.original: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list in its definition, the enumerated value name shall be referenced followed by a non-empty list of integer templates in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template of the form enumerated value name followed by a list of integer templates matches only enumerated values of the same name whose associated integer value is matched by at least one of the integer templates.
requirements.original: The template matches only those enumerated values of the same name where the associated integer values is matched by at least one of the integer templates.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The matching mechanisms of clause B.1.3 MAY be used inside explicit values of strings, record of types, set of types, arrays or maps.
requirements.original: The following matching mechanisms may be used inside explicit values of strings, records of, sets of, arrays or maps.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: A template that contains a matching mechanism inside a value IS called a combined template.
requirements.original: The template that contains a matching mechanism inside a value is called a combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) replaces a single element of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) is used to indicate that it replaces single elements of a string (except character strings, see table 4 for the lengths of the units being matched by "?" in a string), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: The length of the unit matched by AnyElement in a string IS given by table 4.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) is used to indicate that it replaces single elements of a string (except character strings, see table 4 for the lengths of the units being matched by "?" in a string), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of string types, record of types, set of types and arrays.
requirements.original: a) It shall be used only within values of string types, record of types, set of types and arrays.

ambiguity.issue: 'string types' includes character string types, although B.1.3.1.0 and B.1.3.1.1 state that "?" inside character strings is a literal character and that character patterns shall be used instead; chose the reading that excludes character strings.
readings: AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of binary string types (bitstring, hexstring, octetstring), record of types, set of types and arrays.
AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of any string type (including character strings), record of types, set of types and arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: A "?" inside a record of, set of or array value of an integer element type can be interpreted either as AnyValue for the integer element or as AnyElement.
requirements.original: NOTE: The "?" in field4 can be interpreted as AnyValue as an integer value, or AnyElement inside a record of, set of or array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: Interpreting "?" inside a record of, set of or array value as AnyValue or as AnyElement leads to the same matching result.
requirements.original: Since both interpretations lead to the same match no problem arises.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A "?" wildcard in character strings SHALL be expressed using a character pattern.
requirements.original: If it is required to express the "?" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc?xyz"` IS matched by character strings such as "abcdxyz", "abccxyz" and "abcxxyz".
requirements.original: For example: "abcdxyz", "abccxyz", "abcxxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc?xyz".

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc?xyz"` IS NOT matched by character strings such as "abcxyz" and "abcdefxyz".
requirements.original: However, "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz", etc. will not.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: The matching symbol "*" (AnyElementsOrNone) replaces none or any number of consecutive elements of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "*" (AnyElementsOrNone) is used to indicate that it replaces none or any number of consecutive elements of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone matches the longest sequence of elements possible according to the pattern specified by the symbols surrounding the "*".
requirements.original: The "*" symbol matches the longest sequence of elements possible, according to the pattern as specified by the symbols surrounding the "*".

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone in a map template replaces none or any number of elements whose keys are not present in the map template.
requirements.original: _AnyElementsOrNone is also used in templates of a map type where it replaces none or any number of elements whose_ keys are not present in the map template.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: A "*" appearing at the highest level inside a binary string, record of, set of or array value SHALL be interpreted as AnyElementsOrNone.
requirements.original: If a "*" appears at the highest level inside a binary string, a record of, set of or array, it shall be interpreted as _AnyElementsOrNone._

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: A "*" at the highest level inside a binary string, record of, set of or array value IS NOT interpreted as AnyValueOrNone replacing a single element.
requirements.original: NOTE: This rule prevents the otherwise possible interpretation of "*" as AnyValueOrNone that replaces an element inside a binary string, record of, set of or array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be used only within values of binary string types, record of types, set of types, map types and arrays, and inside the permutation matching mechanism.
requirements.original: a) It shall be used only within values of binary string types, record of types, set of, map types and arrays and inside the permutation matching mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A "*" wildcard in character strings SHALL be expressed using a character pattern.
requirements.original: If it is required to expressed the "*" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc*xyz"` IS matched by character strings such as "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz" and "abcabcxyz".
requirements.original: For example: "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz" "abcabcxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc*xyz".

non_requirement.reason: NOTE introduction; the model of implicit decoding is extracted from s011..s018
